---
title: "Audit 4: mutation annotation – Cellosaurus vs the CCLE calls of Shorthouse et al."
author: "Jannik Franken"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
---

## Purpose

Mutation groups define the contrasts of the analysis, so the mutation source
must be reliable and as complete as possible. The use case has so far relied
on Cellosaurus, which lists selected, published variations. Shorthouse et al.
used CCLE mutation calls instead. This notebook compares the two before a
decision is made, and shows how the parsing fix (B1) changed the ranking of the
most frequent mutations used by the original mutation analysis.

**Decision supported:** which mutation source to use (Cellosaurus, the CCLE
calls of Shorthouse et al., or a current DepMap release, which would require a
download).

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/02_cell_lines.tsv`, `02_gene_status.tsv` (Cellosaurus, release 53.0)
- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/Shorthouse_2022.RData`: output of the previous pipeline (`mutated_genes` before the fix)
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_github/Mutations_in_celllines.csv`: mutation calls used by Shorthouse et al. (**local only**, no licence)
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/msb202211006-sup-0005-datasetev4.xlsx`, `…-0006-datasetev5.xlsx`: Datasets EV4/EV5 (genes tested by the authors and their t-statistics)

## Methods

Comparisons were restricted to the 658 genes tested by Shorthouse et al.
(Dataset EV4, derived from the COSMIC Cancer Gene Census), so that passenger
mutations in long genes do not dominate. In the CCLE calls of Shorthouse et
al., a gene counted as mutated if it carried a non-silent variant (missense,
nonsense, frameshift, in-frame insertion/deletion or splice site); silent,
intronic and UTR variants were ignored. The calls combine the sources CCLE,
COSMIC and NCI-60. Cell lines were matched by Cellosaurus name. In Cellosaurus,
a gene counted as mutated if it carried a "Mutation" entry; reported wild type,
deletions and fusions were kept apart. Agreement was assessed on the lines
covered by both sources.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/cellosaurus.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
fig_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_04_mutation_sources")

# cell lines and Cellosaurus status per gene (step 02); the engineered line is left out
cell_lines <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "02_cell_lines.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(!engineered)
gene_status <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "02_gene_status.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(line %in% cell_lines$line)

# genes tested by Shorthouse et al.: the columns of Dataset EV4 ("T_<gene>")
ev4_file <- file.path(raw_dir, "msb202211006-sup-0005-datasetev4.xlsx")
ev4 <- readxl::read_excel(ev4_file, sheet = "Sheet1")
tested_genes <- sub("^T_", "", setdiff(names(ev4), "ionIdx"))
length(tested_genes)
```

## 1. The original mutation analysis before and after the parsing fix

The original analysis (`Mutation_Analyses.Rmd` in the thesis) split
`mutated_genes` into genes and ranked them by the number of lines. Before the
fix, `mutated_genes` also contained genes with a reported wild type, deletions
and fusions.

```{r ranking}
# previous pipeline: genes listed in mutated_genes, per name; names mapped to lines
load_one <- function(f) { e <- new.env(); load(f, envir = e); as.list(e)[[1]] }
old_samples <- load_one(file.path(here::here("data/derived/cancer-cell-lines"), "Shorthouse_2022.RData"))$samples
member_of <- cell_lines %>%
    separate_rows(member_names, sep = "; ") %>%
    select(name = member_names, line)
old_counts <- old_samples %>%
    select(name, mutated_genes) %>%
    inner_join(member_of, by = "name") %>%
    separate_rows(mutated_genes, sep = ";\\s*") %>%
    filter(mutated_genes != "", !is.na(mutated_genes)) %>%
    distinct(line, gene = mutated_genes) %>%
    count(gene, name = "lines_before_fix")

# now: genes with status "mutation"
new_counts <- gene_status %>%
    filter(status == "mutation") %>%
    count(gene, name = "lines_after_fix")

ranking <- full_join(old_counts, new_counts, by = "gene") %>%
    mutate(across(starts_with("lines"), ~ coalesce(.x, 0L))) %>%
    arrange(desc(lines_before_fix)) %>%
    mutate(rank_before = row_number()) %>%
    arrange(desc(lines_after_fix)) %>%
    mutate(rank_after = row_number())
preview_table(arrange(ranking, rank_before), caption = "Lines per gene before and after the fix")

p <- ranking %>%
    filter(rank_before <= 25 | rank_after <= 25) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(lines_before_fix, lines_after_fix), names_to = "version", values_to = "lines") %>%
    mutate(version = recode(version, lines_before_fix = "before fix", lines_after_fix = "after fix")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(lines, reorder(gene, lines), colour = version)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = gene), colour = "grey70") +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("before fix" = "#D55E00", "after fix" = "#0072B2")) +
    labs(x = "Cell lines with the gene counted as mutated", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
         title = "Most frequent mutations in Cellosaurus, before and after the parsing fix",
         subtitle = sprintf("%d cell lines", nrow(cell_lines))) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "ranking_before_after_fix", fig_dir, width = 8, height = 7)
p
```

## 2. Coverage of the two sources

```{r ccle-calls}
# CCLE calls used by Shorthouse et al.; names are Cellosaurus names
calls <- readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "shorthouse_github", "Mutations_in_celllines.csv"),
                         show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet")

# non-silent variants
nonsilent <- calls %>%
    filter(MutationType %in% c("Missense", "Nonsense", "Frame_Shift", "In_Frame") |
               grepl("Splice_Site", MutationType_Raw))

# match names: first to the Cellosaurus name of our lines, then via the general mapping
cellosaurus <- read_cellosaurus(file.path(raw_dir, config$cellosaurus$file))$entries
normalise <- function(x) toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", x))
call_names <- tibble(name = unique(calls$CellLineName_Cellosaurus)) %>%
    mutate(line = cell_lines$line[match(normalise(name), normalise(cell_lines$cellosaurus_name))])
fallback <- map_names_to_accessions(call_names$name[is.na(call_names$line)], cellosaurus)
call_names <- call_names %>%
    left_join(select(fallback, name, ac), by = "name") %>%
    mutate(line = coalesce(line, cell_lines$line[match(ac, cell_lines$accession)])) %>%
    select(name, line)

ccle_status <- nonsilent %>%
    inner_join(filter(call_names, !is.na(line)), by = c("CellLineName_Cellosaurus" = "name")) %>%
    distinct(line, gene = HGNC, source = Source_Type)
ccle_lines <- unique(inner_join(calls, filter(call_names, !is.na(line)),
                                by = c("CellLineName_Cellosaurus" = "name"))$line)
cellosaurus_lines <- unique(gene_status$line)

c(lines = nrow(cell_lines),
  with_cellosaurus_entries = length(cellosaurus_lines),
  with_ccle_calls = length(ccle_lines),
  with_both = length(intersect(ccle_lines, cellosaurus_lines)))

# sources behind the CCLE calls, per line
ccle_status %>% distinct(line, source) %>% count(source)
```

```{r genes-per-line}
# mutated tested genes per line in each source
per_line <- bind_rows(
    gene_status %>% filter(status == "mutation", gene %in% tested_genes) %>%
        count(line) %>% mutate(source = "Cellosaurus"),
    ccle_status %>% filter(gene %in% tested_genes) %>% distinct(line, gene) %>%
        count(line) %>% mutate(source = "CCLE calls (Shorthouse)")
)
per_line %>% group_by(source) %>% summarise(lines = n(), median_genes = median(n), max_genes = max(n))

p <- ggplot(per_line, aes(n, fill = source)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, position = "identity", alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Cellosaurus" = "#E69F00", "CCLE calls (Shorthouse)" = "#0072B2")) +
    labs(x = "Mutated genes per cell line (658 tested genes, log scale)", y = "Cell lines", fill = NULL,
         title = "Cellosaurus lists few mutations per line; the CCLE calls list many") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "genes_per_line_by_source", fig_dir)
p
```

## 3. Agreement per gene

Only lines covered by both sources are used. For each gene, lines are counted
as mutated in both sources, only in Cellosaurus, or only in the CCLE calls.
"Cellosaurus wild type" marks lines where Cellosaurus reports the gene as wild
type but the CCLE calls list a non-silent variant.

```{r agreement}
both_lines <- intersect(ccle_lines, cellosaurus_lines)
cello <- gene_status %>% filter(line %in% both_lines, gene %in% tested_genes)
ccle <- ccle_status %>% filter(line %in% both_lines, gene %in% tested_genes) %>% distinct(line, gene) %>%
    mutate(ccle_mutated = TRUE)

agreement <- full_join(
    cello %>% transmute(line, gene, cellosaurus = status),
    ccle, by = c("line", "gene")
) %>%
    mutate(
        ccle_mutated = coalesce(ccle_mutated, FALSE),
        category = case_when(
            cellosaurus %in% "mutation" & ccle_mutated ~ "both",
            cellosaurus %in% "mutation" ~ "Cellosaurus only",
            cellosaurus %in% "wild_type_reported" & ccle_mutated ~ "Cellosaurus wild type, CCLE mutated",
            ccle_mutated ~ "CCLE only",
            TRUE ~ "neither (other status)"
        )
    )

per_gene <- agreement %>%
    filter(category != "neither (other status)") %>%
    count(gene, category) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
    mutate(total = rowSums(across(-gene))) %>%
    arrange(desc(total))
preview_table(per_gene, caption = sprintf("Agreement per gene (%d lines covered by both)", length(both_lines)))

p <- agreement %>%
    filter(category != "neither (other status)", gene %in% head(per_gene$gene, 30)) %>%
    count(gene, category) %>%
    ggplot(aes(n, reorder(gene, n, sum), fill = category)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("both" = "#009E73", "Cellosaurus only" = "#E69F00",
                                 "CCLE only" = "#0072B2", "Cellosaurus wild type, CCLE mutated" = "#D55E00")) +
    labs(x = "Cell lines", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = "Most mutations in the CCLE calls are missing in Cellosaurus",
         subtitle = sprintf("30 most frequently mutated genes; %d lines covered by both sources", length(both_lines))) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "agreement_per_gene", fig_dir, width = 9, height = 7)
p
```

## 4. Genes of interest in lung

Group sizes for candidate genes in lung lines, by source. The genes are those
discussed in the planning (KRAS, EGFR, STK11, KEAP1 and others) and the genes
Shorthouse et al. analysed in lung (KEAP1, NFE2L2, STK11; Appendix Fig S6).

```{r lung}
genes_of_interest <- c("TP53", "KRAS", "EGFR", "STK11", "KEAP1", "NFE2L2", "CDKN2A",
                       "SMARCA4", "PIK3CA", "BRAF", "NRAS", "PTEN", "IDH1", "IDH2")
lung <- cell_lines$line[cell_lines$tissue %in% "Lung"]
lung_both <- intersect(lung, both_lines)

lung_counts <- bind_rows(
    gene_status %>% filter(line %in% lung, status == "mutation") %>% count(gene) %>%
        mutate(source = sprintf("Cellosaurus (%d lung lines)", length(lung))),
    gene_status %>% filter(line %in% lung_both, status == "mutation") %>% count(gene) %>%
        mutate(source = sprintf("Cellosaurus, lines with CCLE calls (%d)", length(lung_both))),
    ccle_status %>% filter(line %in% lung_both) %>% distinct(line, gene) %>% count(gene) %>%
        mutate(source = sprintf("CCLE calls, same lines (%d)", length(lung_both)))
) %>%
    filter(gene %in% genes_of_interest) %>%
    complete(gene = genes_of_interest, source, fill = list(n = 0))

lung_counts %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = n) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Mutated lung lines per gene and source")

p <- ggplot(lung_counts, aes(n, factor(gene, levels = rev(genes_of_interest)), fill = source)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E69F00", "#F0E442", "#0072B2")) +
    labs(x = "Mutated lung lines", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = "Lung: mutated lines per gene by source") +
    theme_uc() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
save_figure(p, "lung_genes_by_source", fig_dir, width = 8, height = 6.5)
p
```

## 5. Reference results of Shorthouse et al. (EV4, EV5)

Dataset EV4 holds, for every ion and tested gene, the t-statistic of a
regression of the metabolite level on mutation status with tissue as
covariate. Dataset EV5 repeats this for individual KRAS variants. They are a
reference for later comparisons and for positive controls.

```{r ev4}
ev5 <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(raw_dir, "msb202211006-sup-0006-datasetev5.xlsx"), sheet = "Sheet1")
c(ev4_ions = nrow(ev4), ev4_genes = length(tested_genes),
  ev5_ions = nrow(ev5), ev5_kras_variants = ncol(ev5) - 1)
names(ev5)[-1]

# number of ions with |t| > 5 (the threshold used in the authors' Appendix Fig S6)
ev4_strong <- tibble(
    gene = tested_genes,
    ions_abs_t_above_5 = colSums(abs(as.matrix(ev4[, paste0("T_", tested_genes)])) > 5, na.rm = TRUE)
) %>% arrange(desc(ions_abs_t_above_5))
ev4_strong %>% filter(gene %in% genes_of_interest)
preview_table(ev4_strong, caption = "Ions with |t| > 5 per gene (EV4)")
```

## 6. DepMap 24Q4

DepMap 24Q4 Public (Figshare, doi:10.25452/figshare.plus.27993248.v1, CC BY 4.0;
**local only**, `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/depmap_24Q4/`) provides Mutect2
somatic calls of protein-changing variants with annotation, and gene-level
absolute copy number (PureCN). Two definitions of a mutated gene are used:
**any** protein-changing variant (comparable to the CCLE calls), and **likely
driver**: a variant flagged by DepMap as hotspot (Hess et al. 2019, OncoKB,
COSMIC tier 1), likely loss of function, Hess driver, or high-impact in an
oncogene or tumour suppressor. A gene counts as deleted at absolute copy number
0. Lines are matched through the RRID of the DepMap model table, i.e. directly
by Cellosaurus accession.

```{r depmap-load}
depmap_dir <- file.path(raw_dir, "depmap_24Q4")
stopifnot(dir.exists(depmap_dir))

# DepMap models matched to our lines by RRID (= Cellosaurus accession)
models <- readr::read_csv(file.path(depmap_dir, "Model.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    select(ModelID, RRID, CellLineName, OncotreeLineage)
model_of_line <- cell_lines %>%
    inner_join(models, by = c("accession" = "RRID")) %>%
    distinct(line, ModelID)
c(lines = nrow(cell_lines), matched_to_depmap = n_distinct(model_of_line$line),
  lines_with_several_models = sum(table(model_of_line$line) > 1))

# somatic calls of the matched models
depmap_calls <- data.table::fread(
    file.path(depmap_dir, "OmicsSomaticMutations.csv"),
    select = c("ModelID", "HugoSymbol", "ProteinChange", "VariantInfo", "Hotspot", "LikelyLoF",
               "HessDriver", "OncogeneHighImpact", "TumorSuppressorHighImpact")
) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    inner_join(model_of_line, by = "ModelID", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    mutate(likely_driver = Hotspot | LikelyLoF | HessDriver | OncogeneHighImpact | TumorSuppressorHighImpact)

depmap_status <- depmap_calls %>%
    group_by(line, gene = HugoSymbol) %>%
    summarise(any = TRUE, likely_driver = any(likely_driver), .groups = "drop")
depmap_lines <- unique(model_of_line$line)
```

```{r depmap-genes-per-line}
# mutated tested genes per line, now with both DepMap definitions
per_line_all <- bind_rows(
    per_line,
    depmap_status %>% filter(gene %in% tested_genes) %>% count(line) %>% mutate(source = "DepMap, any"),
    depmap_status %>% filter(gene %in% tested_genes, likely_driver) %>% count(line) %>%
        mutate(source = "DepMap, likely driver")
)
per_line_all %>% group_by(source) %>% summarise(lines = n(), median_genes = median(n), max_genes = max(n))

# genes the CCLE calls list as mutated in most lines: does DepMap agree?
suspicious <- c("CLTCL1", "MAP3K1", "RECQL4", "MUC16", "LRP1B", "CSMD3")
common_lines <- Reduce(intersect, list(ccle_lines, depmap_lines, cellosaurus_lines))
tibble(gene = suspicious) %>%
    mutate(
        ccle_calls = sapply(gene, function(g) n_distinct(ccle_status$line[ccle_status$gene == g & ccle_status$line %in% common_lines])),
        depmap_any = sapply(gene, function(g) sum(depmap_status$gene == g & depmap_status$line %in% common_lines)),
        depmap_likely_driver = sapply(gene, function(g) sum(depmap_status$gene == g & depmap_status$likely_driver & depmap_status$line %in% common_lines))
    ) %>%
    mutate(lines_compared = length(common_lines))
```

```{r depmap-lung}
# lung group sizes for the genes of interest, all sources on the same lines
lung_common <- intersect(lung, common_lines)
count_lines <- function(lines_mutated) sapply(genes_of_interest, function(g) length(intersect(lines_mutated(g), lung_common)))
lung_sources <- tibble(
    gene = genes_of_interest,
    Cellosaurus = count_lines(function(g) gene_status$line[gene_status$gene == g & gene_status$status == "mutation"]),
    `CCLE calls (Shorthouse)` = count_lines(function(g) ccle_status$line[ccle_status$gene == g]),
    `DepMap, any` = count_lines(function(g) depmap_status$line[depmap_status$gene == g]),
    `DepMap, likely driver` = count_lines(function(g) depmap_status$line[depmap_status$gene == g & depmap_status$likely_driver])
)
preview_table(lung_sources, caption = sprintf("Mutated lung lines per gene and source (%d lung lines covered by all sources)", length(lung_common)))

p <- lung_sources %>%
    pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "source", values_to = "n") %>%
    mutate(source = factor(source, levels = names(lung_sources)[-1])) %>%
    ggplot(aes(n, factor(gene, levels = rev(genes_of_interest)), fill = source)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E69F00", "#0072B2", "#009E73", "#CC79A7")) +
    labs(x = "Mutated lung lines", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = "Lung: mutated lines per gene, four sources on the same lines",
         subtitle = sprintf("%d lung lines covered by Cellosaurus, CCLE calls and DepMap", length(lung_common))) +
    theme_uc() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
save_figure(p, "lung_genes_four_sources", fig_dir, width = 9, height = 6.5)
p

# agreement for the main drivers between Cellosaurus and DepMap (all lines covered by both)
both_cd <- intersect(cellosaurus_lines, depmap_lines)
bind_rows(lapply(c("TP53", "KRAS", "EGFR", "BRAF", "PIK3CA", "STK11", "KEAP1"), function(g) {
    cel <- gene_status$line[gene_status$gene == g & gene_status$status == "mutation"]
    dep <- depmap_status$line[depmap_status$gene == g]
    tibble(gene = g, both = length(intersect(intersect(cel, dep), both_cd)),
           cellosaurus_only = length(intersect(setdiff(cel, dep), both_cd)),
           depmap_only = length(intersect(setdiff(dep, cel), both_cd)))
})) %>% mutate(lines_compared = length(both_cd))
```

```{r depmap-deletions}
# homozygous deletions (absolute copy number 0) for genes relevant to the planning
cn_header <- names(data.table::fread(file.path(depmap_dir, "OmicsAbsoluteCNGene.csv"), nrows = 0))
deletion_genes <- c("CDKN2A", "MTAP", "PTEN", "SMAD4", "STK11", "RB1")
cn_cols <- cn_header[sub(" \\(.*$", "", cn_header) %in% deletion_genes]
cn <- data.table::fread(file.path(depmap_dir, "OmicsAbsoluteCNGene.csv"), select = c(cn_header[1], cn_cols)) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    rename(ModelID = 1) %>%
    inner_join(model_of_line, by = "ModelID") %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(cn_cols), names_to = "gene", values_to = "cn") %>%
    mutate(gene = sub(" \\(.*$", "", gene))

cn_lines <- unique(cn$line)
cello_del <- gene_status %>% filter(status == "deletion")
cn %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(
        lines_with_copy_number = n_distinct(line),
        depmap_deleted = n_distinct(line[cn == 0 & !is.na(cn)]),
        cellosaurus_deleted = n_distinct(intersect(cello_del$line[cello_del$gene == first(gene)], cn_lines)),
        both = n_distinct(intersect(line[cn == 0 & !is.na(cn)], cello_del$line[cello_del$gene == first(gene)])),
        depmap_deleted_in_lung = n_distinct(intersect(line[cn == 0 & !is.na(cn)], lung)),
        .groups = "drop"
    )
```

## Interpretation and proposed decision

- **Ranking of the original analysis:** after the parsing fix, TP53 drops from
  150 to 132 mutated lines and CDKN2A from 27 to 13 (most entries were
  deletions); the order of the other frequent genes barely changes.
- **Coverage:** Cellosaurus lists a median of 2 mutated tested genes per line,
  the CCLE calls 24. For the classical drivers both agree well (TP53: 121 lines
  in both, 7 in only one source; KRAS: 41 in both, 1 only in CCLE).
- **Cellosaurus misses most co-mutations.** In lung, KEAP1 is mutated in 12
  lines according to the CCLE calls but in 1 according to Cellosaurus; STK11
  16 vs 4, SMARCA4 20 vs 4, NFE2L2 5 vs 0. These are exactly the co-mutations
  planned as covariates (e.g. STK11/KEAP1 for KRAS in lung) and the positive
  controls analysed by Shorthouse et al. (Appendix Fig S6). With Cellosaurus,
  absent entries would be read as wild type and the covariates would be wrong.
- **The CCLE calls of Shorthouse et al. are not a clean alternative either:**
  they mix three sources (CCLE, COSMIC, NCI-60) and count every non-silent
  variant, so genes such as CLTCL1, MAP3K1 or RECQL4 appear mutated in most
  lines, which suggests passenger variants or artefacts rather than drivers.
  The file also comes from an unlicensed repository.
- **Reference results:** EV4 reports many ions with |t| > 5 for KRAS, BRAF,
  PIK3CA, TP53 and STK11, and also for KEAP1 and NFE2L2, which supports these
  genes as candidates and positive controls.

- **DepMap 24Q4** matches 169 of 174 lines directly by RRID. For the main
  drivers it agrees with Cellosaurus (KRAS: 43 lines in both, none in only
  one; TP53: 127 in both, 4 + 4 in only one), and it captures the
  co-mutations Cellosaurus misses (lung, 83 lines covered by all sources:
  STK11 20 vs 3, KEAP1 16 vs 1, SMARCA4 21 vs 4, NFE2L2 5 vs 0).
- The genes that the CCLE calls of Shorthouse et al. list as mutated in most
  lines (CLTCL1 128 lines, MAP3K1 106, RECQL4 101) are rare in DepMap (7, 3, 3),
  which confirms that those calls contain artefacts or mixed-source noise.
- DepMap's "likely driver" flag is stricter: it keeps KRAS and TP53 but drops
  many KEAP1 missense variants (7 of 16 lung lines kept). Which definition to
  use per gene is a design question for the contrast selection (Phase 3).
- **Deletions:** DepMap copy number shows homozygous CDKN2A deletion in 51 and
  MTAP deletion in 34 of 138 lines; Cellosaurus lists 11 and 0. MTAP, a
  positive-control genotype in the planning, is only available from DepMap.

**Decision (2026-10-28):** DepMap 24Q4 (Figshare, CC BY 4.0, citable DOI) is
the source of mutation and copy-number status, matched by RRID; Cellosaurus
stays for cell line identity (accessions) and as a documented cross-check. The
per-gene definition of "mutated" (any protein-changing vs likely driver) is
fixed when the contrasts are chosen (Phase 3).

sessionInfo()
